questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :
कथन-I : 1985 में सोवियत संघ की कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के महासचिव बने मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव ने सोवियत प्रणाली में सुधार की कोशिश की ।
कथन-II : पश्चिम के साथ संबंधों को सामान्य बनाने, सोवियत संघ को लोकतांत्रिक बनाने और सुधारने जैसे गोर्बाचेव के फैसलों के कुछ अन्य प्रभाव हुए जिनका गोर्बाचेव या अन्य किसी को न तो अंदाजा था न ही इरादा था ।
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : Mikhail Gorbachev, who had become General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1985, sought to reform the Soviet System.
Statement-II : Gorbachev's decision to normalise relations with the West and democratise and reform the Soviet Union had some other effects that neither he nor anyone else intended or anticipated.

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं ।
options.C: कथन I सत्य है, लेकिन कथन II असत्य है ।
options.D: कथन I असत्य है, लेकिन कथन II सत्य है ।

options_english.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options_english.C: Statement-I is true, but Statement-II is false.
options_english.D: Statement-I is false, but Statement-II is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Statement-I is historically accurate: Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary of the CPSU in 1985 and launched his famous reforms of glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) to revitalise the Soviet system. Statement-II is equally correct: Gorbachev's reforms had unintended consequences — they unleashed forces that ultimately led to the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991, an outcome that nobody, including Gorbachev himself, had anticipated or intended.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं। कथन-I ऐतिहासिक रूप से सत्य है: मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव 1985 में CPSU के महासचिव बने और उन्होंने ग्लासनोस्त तथा पेरेस्त्रोइका जैसे सुधार शुरू किए। कथन-II भी सही है: इन सुधारों के अनपेक्षित परिणाम हुए जिनके कारण 1991 में सोवियत संघ का विघटन हो गया, जो किसी ने नहीं सोचा था।
questions.topic: Gorbachev's Reforms and Disintegration of USSR

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन पूँजीवादी और साम्यवादी दुनिया के बीच विभाजन का प्रतीक था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following symbolised the division between the Capitalist and the Communist world ?
questions.solution: The Berlin Wall, constructed in 1961, was the most powerful physical and symbolic representation of the division between the capitalist West (West Berlin/NATO bloc) and the communist East (East Berlin/Warsaw Pact). It literally divided a city and a nation into two ideological camps. The Gulf War, First World War, and Second World War are military conflicts and do not symbolise the ideological divide between capitalism and communism in the same direct manner.
questions.solution_hindi: बर्लिन की दीवार 1961 में बनाई गई थी और यह पूँजीवादी पश्चिम तथा साम्यवादी पूर्व के बीच सबसे शक्तिशाली भौतिक और प्रतीकात्मक विभाजन का प्रतीक थी। इसने एक शहर और एक राष्ट्र को दो विचारधाराओं में विभाजित किया।

questions.text: कॉलम A में दिए गए पदों का कॉलम B के साथ सही मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूट से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Match the terms given in Column-A correctly with Column-B and choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
questions.solution: The correct matching is: (a) Balance of Power — (iii) Traditional security, because maintaining a balance of power among states is a classic concept of traditional or conventional security; (b) Disarmament — (i) Giving up certain types of weapons, as disarmament literally means reducing or eliminating weapons; (c) Migration — (iv) New source of threat, because large-scale migration is identified as a non-traditional or new security challenge; (d) Freedom from threats — (ii) Security, because security in its broadest sense means being free from threats. Hence Option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही मिलान है: (a) शक्ति संतुलन — (iii) पारंपरिक सुरक्षा; (b) निरस्त्रीकरण — (i) कुछ विशेष प्रकार के हथियारों को छोड़ना; (c) प्रवासन — (iv) खतरे का नया स्रोत; (d) खतरों से आज़ादी — (ii) सुरक्षा। अतः विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित को उनके घटित होने के कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) भारत-चीन युद्ध
(ii) भारत का प्रथम परमाणु परीक्षण
(iii) आतंकवादियों द्वारा अमरीका में वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर पर हमला
(iv) एंटी-बैलेस्टिक मिसाइल संधि
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their happening :
(i) India-China War
(ii) India's first test of a nuclear device
(iii) Terrorists attack on World Trade Centre in America
(iv) The Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is: (i) India-China War — 1962; (iv) Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty — 1972; (ii) India's first nuclear test (Pokhran-I / Smiling Buddha) — 1974; (iii) Terrorist attack on World Trade Centre — 2001. Therefore the correct sequence is (i), (iv), (ii), (iii), which corresponds to Option D.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम: (i) भारत-चीन युद्ध — 1962; (iv) एंटी-बैलेस्टिक मिसाइल संधि — 1972; (ii) भारत का पहला परमाणु परीक्षण — 1974; (iii) वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर पर हमला — 2001। अतः सही क्रम (i), (iv), (ii), (iii) है जो विकल्प D है।
questions.chapter: Security in Contemporary World / India's External Relations

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प ग्रीन हाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन को कम करने के लिए था ?
questions.text_english: Which one among the following agreements was to cut the green house gas emissions ?
questions.solution: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) was a landmark international agreement that required industrialised countries to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. It operationalised the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and set binding emission reduction targets. The Montreal Protocol deals with ozone-depleting substances, not greenhouse gases directly. The Antarctic Treaty and Antarctic Environmental Protocol deal with scientific cooperation and environmental protection in Antarctica, not with greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.solution_hindi: क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल (1997) एक महत्वपूर्ण अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समझौता था जिसमें औद्योगिक देशों को ग्रीन हाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन को कम करना था। मॉन्ट्रियल प्रोटोकॉल ओजोन परत क्षरण से संबंधित है, अंटार्कटिक संधि और अंटार्कटिक पर्यावरणीय प्रोटोकॉल अंटार्कटिका से संबंधित हैं।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न में दो कथनों को क्रमश: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है । उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
अभिकथन (A) : 1975 में आपातकाल के दौरान सरकार ने प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता को निलंबित कर दिया और प्रेस सेंसरशिप लागू कर दी ।
कारण (R) : समाचार-पत्रों ने केवल कार्टून दिखाकर सेंसरशिप का विरोध किया ।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the appropriate option as correct answer :
Assertion (A) : The government suspended the freedom of press and implemented press censorship during emergency in 1975.
Reason (R) : Newspapers protested against censorship by showing the cartoons only.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है ।

options_english.A: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, but the Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: The Assertion (A) is incorrect, but the Reason (R) is correct.
options_english.D: The Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is correct: during the Emergency of 1975, Indira Gandhi's government suspended press freedom and imposed strict censorship. Reason (R) is also correct: some newspapers did leave their editorial columns blank or printed only cartoons as a silent protest against censorship. However, R is not the correct explanation of A, because press censorship was imposed for political reasons — to suppress opposition and critical reporting — not because newspapers were printing cartoons. The two statements describe different independent facts. Hence Option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) सही है: 1975 के आपातकाल में प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता निलंबित कर दी गई थी। कारण (R) भी सही है: कुछ समाचार-पत्रों ने केवल कार्टून दिखाकर विरोध किया। परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है क्योंकि सेंसरशिप राजनीतिक कारणों से लगाई गई थी। अतः विकल्प B सही है।

questions.text: भारत की परमाणु नीति के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से सही कथन का चुनाव कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Choose the correct statement about India's nuclear policy from the statements given below :

options.A: भारत का परमाणु कार्यक्रम 1952 में होमी जे. भाभा के मार्गदर्शन में आरम्भ किया गया था ।
options.B: भारत NPT के समर्थन में था ।
options.C: अब भारत ने स्पष्ट कर दिया है कि 'पहले उपयोग नहीं' की नीति की समीक्षा की जा सकती है ।
options.D: नेहरू परमाणु हथियारों के खिलाफ नहीं थे ।

options_english.A: India's nuclear programme was started in 1952 under the guidance of Homi J. Bhabha.
options_english.B: India was in support of the NPT.
options_english.C: Now India has made it clear that the policy of 'no first use' can be reviewed.
options_english.D: Nehru was not against nuclear weapons.

questions.solution: India's nuclear programme was indeed established in 1948 (formally set up under the Atomic Energy Commission) with Homi J. Bhabha as its guiding figure, and the first nuclear research activities began around 1948–1954 under his leadership, so the statement in Option A closely reflects this historical fact. Option B is incorrect because India has consistently opposed the NPT as discriminatory. Option C is incorrect because India officially maintains a 'no first use' policy without formally saying it is under review (although there has been debate, no clear official statement has been made to this effect as an established policy). Option D is incorrect because Nehru was famously against nuclear weapons and advocated global disarmament.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत का परमाणु कार्यक्रम होमी जे. भाभा के नेतृत्व में शुरू हुआ था। भारत NPT का विरोधी रहा है क्योंकि यह भेदभावपूर्ण है। 'पहले उपयोग नहीं' नीति भारत की आधिकारिक नीति है। नेहरू परमाणु हथियारों के विरुद्ध थे। अतः सही उत्तर A है।

questions.text: भारत का कौन सा राजनीतिक दल चाहता था कि भारत अमरीका समर्थक विदेश नीति का पालन करे ?
questions.text_english: Which political party of India wanted India to follow a pro-US foreign policy ?
questions.solution: The Bharatiya Jan Sangh was the political party that favoured a pro-US foreign policy for India during the Cold War era. It was critical of Nehru's Non-Alignment policy and believed India should align with the Western capitalist bloc led by the USA. In contrast, the Communist Party of India favoured closer ties with the Soviet Union, while the Congress Party under Nehru championed Non-Alignment, and the Socialist Party also broadly supported Non-Alignment.
questions.solution_hindi: भारतीय जन संघ वह दल था जो चाहता था कि भारत अमेरिका समर्थक विदेश नीति अपनाए। यह नेहरू की गुटनिरपेक्षता नीति का विरोधी था। कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी सोवियत संघ की समर्थक थी जबकि कांग्रेस ने गुटनिरपेक्षता को अपनाया। अतः सही उत्तर A है।
questions.topic: Political Parties and Foreign Policy Debate

questions.text: कौन सी राजनीतिक पार्टी ने भारत के पहले आम चुनाव में लोकसभा की 16 सीटें जीतीं और दूसरे स्थान पर रही ?
questions.text_english: Which political party won 16 Lok Sabha seats and was at second place in the first General Election of India ?
questions.solution: In India's first General Election of 1951–52, the Indian National Congress won an overwhelming majority. The Communist Party of India (CPI) came second with 16 Lok Sabha seats, making it the single largest opposition party in the first Lok Sabha. The Bharatiya Jan Sangh, the Socialist Party, and the Swatantra Party (which was formed only in 1959) did not achieve this standing in the first election.
questions.solution_hindi: 1951-52 के पहले आम चुनाव में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने भारी बहुमत जीता। कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया 16 सीटें जीतकर दूसरे स्थान पर रही। अतः सही उत्तर A है।

questions.text: ई.वी.एम. का सही विस्तृत रूप चुनिए ।
questions.text_english: Choose the correct full form of the EVM.
questions.solution: EVM stands for Electronic Voting Machine. It is a device used in Indian elections to record votes electronically, replacing the traditional paper ballot system. It was first used on a pilot basis in 1982 and has been used in all general elections since 2004. The other options — Electric, Easy, and Election — are incorrect expansions of the abbreviation.
questions.solution_hindi: EVM का पूर्ण रूप 'इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वोटिंग मशीन' है। इसका उपयोग भारतीय चुनावों में मतदान को इलेक्ट्रॉनिक रूप से दर्ज करने के लिए किया जाता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं। अतः सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text: 1975 में भारत में आपातकाल की घोषणा निम्नलिखित में से किस आधार पर की गई थी ?
questions.text_english: On which one of the following basis was emergency declared in 1975 ?
questions.solution: The Emergency of June 1975 was declared by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on the grounds of 'internal disturbances' under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution. It was not declared due to external aggression or armed rebellion. The claim of internal disturbance was used to justify the crackdown on political opposition and civil liberties. Later, the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with the more specific term 'armed rebellion' to prevent such misuse.
questions.solution_hindi: जून 1975 में आपातकाल की घोषणा 'आंतरिक गड़बड़ी' के आधार पर संविधान के अनुच्छेद 352 के तहत की गई थी। बाद में 44वें संशोधन द्वारा 'आंतरिक गड़बड़ी' को 'सशस्त्र विद्रोह' से बदल दिया गया। अतः सही उत्तर A है।

questions.text: कौन से देश में ऑस्ट्रेलियाई खनन कंपनी 'वेस्टर्न माइनिंग कॉर्पोरेशन (WMC)' का विरोध किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: In which country was an Australian Mining Company 'WMC' opposed ?
questions.solution: The Western Mining Corporation (WMC), an Australian mining company, faced strong opposition in the Philippines. Local communities and indigenous peoples' groups protested against WMC's mining operations in the country, raising concerns about environmental damage and violation of indigenous land rights. This case is often cited as an example of resistance against multinational corporations exploiting natural resources in developing countries.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑस्ट्रेलियाई खनन कंपनी 'वेस्टर्न माइनिंग कॉर्पोरेशन (WMC)' का विरोध फिलीपींस में किया गया था। स्थानीय समुदायों ने पर्यावरण क्षति और आदिवासी भूमि अधिकारों के उल्लंघन के कारण विरोध किया। अतः सही उत्तर B है।

questions.text: 'आसियान' के किन्हीं दो प्रमुख उद्देश्यों को लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: State any two main objectives of 'ASEAN'.

key_points: To accelerate economic growth, social progress and cultural development in the region
To promote regional peace and stability through respect for justice and the rule of law
key_points_hindi: क्षेत्र में आर्थिक विकास, सामाजिक प्रगति और सांस्कृतिक विकास को गति देना
न्याय और कानून के शासन के सम्मान के माध्यम से क्षेत्रीय शांति और स्थिरता को बढ़ावा देना

questions.solution: ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) was established in 1967 with the signing of the Bangkok Declaration. Two of its main objectives are: first, to accelerate economic growth, social progress, and cultural development among its member states through joint endeavours, thereby strengthening the foundation for a prosperous and peaceful community; and second, to promote regional peace and stability by fostering respect for justice and the rule of law in the relationships among member nations, as well as adherence to the principles of the United Nations Charter.
questions.solution_hindi: आसियान (दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई राष्ट्रों का संघ) की स्थापना 1967 में बैंकॉक घोषणा के साथ हुई। इसके दो प्रमुख उद्देश्य हैं: प्रथम, सदस्य देशों में आर्थिक वृद्धि, सामाजिक प्रगति और सांस्कृतिक विकास को संयुक्त प्रयासों से गति देना; द्वितीय, सदस्य देशों के बीच न्याय, कानून के शासन और संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर के सिद्धांतों के प्रति सम्मान को बढ़ावा देकर क्षेत्रीय शांति और स्थिरता को सुदृढ़ करना।

questions.text: 'कांग्रेस पार्टी के प्रभुत्व काल के दौरान इसके नेताओं ने अन्य नई पार्टियाँ बनाने की कभी कोई इच्छा नहीं दिखाई ।' इसके किसी एक कारण का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: 'During the period of dominance of the Congress Party, its leaders never showed any desire to form new parties.' Analyse any one reason for this.

key_points: The Congress was an umbrella organisation that accommodated diverse ideological groups within itself
Leaders with differing views could express dissent within the party rather than leaving to form a new one
key_points_hindi: कांग्रेस एक छाता संगठन था जो विभिन्न विचारधाराओं को अपने भीतर समाहित करता था
मतभेद रखने वाले नेता पार्टी के भीतर ही असहमति व्यक्त कर सकते थे

questions.solution: During the Congress dominance era, the party functioned as a broad umbrella organisation that accommodated diverse groups — socialists, conservatives, liberals, and moderates — under a single platform. Leaders who disagreed with party policies could form pressure groups and factions within the Congress itself and influence decision-making from inside. Since the party was large enough to offer political space to ideologically different leaders, there was no need to form separate parties. This internal accommodation of diversity kept potential dissenters within the fold rather than pushing them to create rival organisations.
questions.solution_hindi: कांग्रेस प्रभुत्व काल में पार्टी एक व्यापक छाता संगठन के रूप में कार्य करती थी जो समाजवादी, रूढ़िवादी और उदारवादी विभिन्न विचारधाराओं को अपने भीतर स्थान देती थी। असहमत नेता पार्टी के भीतर ही दबाव समूह या गुट बनाकर नीति निर्माण को प्रभावित कर सकते थे। इस आंतरिक समायोजन के कारण नेताओं को अलग पार्टी बनाने की आवश्यकता नहीं पड़ी।

questions.text: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना और द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना के बीच कोई दो अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two differences between the First Five Year Plan and Second Five Year Plan.

key_points: First Plan focused on agriculture and land reforms; Second Plan emphasised heavy industries
First Plan (1951–56) had modest targets suitable for post-Partition reconstruction; Second Plan (1956–61) was more ambitious following the Mahalanobis model
key_points_hindi: प्रथम योजना में कृषि और भूमि सुधार पर जोर; द्वितीय योजना में भारी उद्योगों पर बल
प्रथम योजना विनम्र लक्ष्यों वाली थी; द्वितीय योजना महालनोबिस मॉडल पर आधारित महत्वाकांक्षी योजना थी

questions.solution: The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) prioritised agriculture, land reforms, and irrigation, aiming at food security and post-Partition rehabilitation of the economy. In contrast, the Second Five Year Plan (1956–61), based on the Mahalanobis model, shifted focus to rapid industrialisation, especially the development of heavy industries like steel and iron. Additionally, the First Plan had modest financial targets appropriate for a newly independent nation recovering from Partition, while the Second Plan was far more ambitious in scope, seeking to transform India's industrial base and was more influenced by socialist planning principles.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना (1951-56) में कृषि, भूमि सुधार और सिंचाई पर जोर दिया गया था ताकि खाद्य सुरक्षा और बंटवारे के बाद की पुनर्बहाली सुनिश्चित हो। इसके विपरीत, द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) महालनोबिस मॉडल पर आधारित थी और इसमें भारी उद्योगों, विशेषकर इस्पात उद्योग, पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया गया। इसके अलावा, प्रथम योजना के वित्तीय लक्ष्य सीमित थे जबकि द्वितीय योजना कहीं अधिक महत्वाकांक्षी थी।

questions.text: 1979 में जनता पार्टी में विभाजन के किन्हीं दो कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two reasons for the split in the Janta Party in 1979.

key_points: Internal power struggle and conflict among leaders like Charan Singh, Jagjivan Ram, and Morarji Desai
Lack of a common ideology and programme — the party was an opportunistic alliance of anti-Congress groups
key_points_hindi: नेताओं के बीच आंतरिक सत्ता संघर्ष
साझा विचारधारा का अभाव — पार्टी अवसरवादी गठजोड़ थी

questions.solution: The Janta Party, which came to power in 1977 defeating the Congress after the Emergency, split in 1979 for two major reasons. First, there were intense personal rivalries and power struggles among top leaders — Morarji Desai, Charan Singh, and Jagjivan Ram — each of whom wanted to lead the government and party, making coordination impossible. Second, the Janta Party had no common ideology; it was merely an opportunistic coalition of diverse anti-Congress groups including socialists, Hindu nationalists, and conservatives, who had united only to defeat Indira Gandhi. Once in power, their ideological differences resurfaced and could not be reconciled.
questions.solution_hindi: 1977 में आपातकाल के बाद कांग्रेस को हराकर सत्ता में आई जनता पार्टी 1979 में दो प्रमुख कारणों से टूट गई। प्रथम, मोरारजी देसाई, चरण सिंह और जगजीवन राम जैसे नेताओं के बीच व्यक्तिगत प्रतिद्वंद्विता और सत्ता संघर्ष था। द्वितीय, पार्टी में कोई साझा विचारधारा नहीं थी; यह केवल कांग्रेस विरोधी विभिन्न गुटों का अवसरवादी गठजोड़ था जो सत्ता में आने के बाद बिखर गया।

questions.text: वैश्विक स्तर पर गरीब और अमीर देशों के बीच आर्थिक असमानता को कम करने के कोई दो तरीके सुझाइए ।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two ways to reduce economic disparity between the poor and the rich countries at the global level.

key_points: Establishing a New International Economic Order (NIEO) that ensures fair terms of trade for developing countries
Increasing development aid from rich nations and reforming international institutions like the IMF and World Bank to give greater voting rights to developing countries
key_points_hindi: विकासशील देशों के लिए उचित व्यापार शर्तों को सुनिश्चित करने वाली नई अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आर्थिक व्यवस्था की स्थापना
विकसित देशों द्वारा विकास सहायता बढ़ाना और IMF व विश्व बैंक में सुधार

questions.solution: Two important ways to reduce economic disparity between poor and rich countries at the global level are: first, establishing a New International Economic Order (NIEO) that provides developing nations with fair terms of trade, better prices for their exports, reduced trade barriers in rich countries, and access to technology — as demanded by the Group of 77 developing nations in the 1970s; and second, reforming global financial institutions such as the IMF and the World Bank to give developing countries greater representation and voting power, thereby ensuring that these institutions serve the genuine developmental needs of poorer nations rather than the interests of wealthy ones.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्विक स्तर पर आर्थिक असमानता कम करने के दो तरीके: प्रथम, विकासशील देशों को उचित व्यापार शर्तें, निर्यात के बेहतर मूल्य और प्रौद्योगिकी तक पहुँच प्रदान करने वाली नई अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आर्थिक व्यवस्था (NIEO) की स्थापना; द्वितीय, IMF और विश्व बैंक जैसी वैश्विक वित्तीय संस्थाओं में सुधार करके विकासशील देशों को अधिक प्रतिनिधित्व और मतदान अधिकार देना।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ और अमरीका के बीच अस्त्र नियंत्रण के लिए हस्ताक्षरित किन्हीं दो सन्धियों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: State any two arms control treaties signed between the US and Soviet Union.

key_points: SALT-I (Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty-I, 1972)
SALT-II (Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty-II, 1979) / START (Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty)

questions.solution: Two major arms control treaties signed between the United States and the Soviet Union are: first, the SALT-I (Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty, 1972), signed during the detente period between Nixon and Brezhnev, which placed limits on the number of nuclear missiles and launchers each side could possess; and second, the SALT-II (1979), signed between Carter and Brezhnev, which further restricted the development of new strategic nuclear weapons, though it was never formally ratified by the US Senate due to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. Another significant treaty was the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty of 1972, which limited defensive missile systems.
questions.solution_hindi: अमेरिका और सोवियत संघ के बीच हस्ताक्षरित दो प्रमुख अस्त्र नियंत्रण संधियाँ: प्रथम, SALT-I (1972) — यह शीतयुद्ध के दौरान तनाव शैथिल्य काल में हस्ताक्षरित हुई जिसने परमाणु मिसाइलों की संख्या को सीमित किया; द्वितीय, SALT-II (1979) — इसने नई रणनीतिक परमाणु हथियार प्रणालियों के विकास पर अंकुश लगाया। एंटी-बैलेस्टिक मिसाइल संधि (1972) भी एक महत्वपूर्ण संधि थी।

अथवा
(b) "चीन की अर्थव्यवस्था में सुधार हुआ है लेकिन वहाँ हर किसी को सुधारों का लाभ नहीं मिला ।" इसके किन्हीं दो कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse the basis of projecting China to overtake the US America to become the world's largest economy.
OR
(b) "While the Chinese economy has improved, not everyone in China received the benefits of the reforms." Analyse any two reasons for this.

key_points: (a) China's sustained high GDP growth rate over several decades
(a) China's massive manufacturing base and export-led growth model
(a) Huge population providing large labour force and growing domestic market
(b) Rising inequality between urban and rural areas
(b) Benefits concentrated among coastal regions and elite classes

questions.solution:
Answer (a): China's projection to overtake the United States as the world's largest economy rests on several strong foundations. China has consistently maintained one of the highest GDP growth rates in the world over the past four decades, averaging around 9–10% annually since its reforms began in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. China has built the world's largest manufacturing sector, becoming the global factory for goods ranging from electronics to textiles, which has driven massive export-led growth. Its enormous population of over 1.4 billion provides both a vast labour force that keeps production costs competitive and a rapidly expanding domestic consumer market. China has also accumulated huge foreign exchange reserves and has become the world's largest trading nation. Economic projections from institutions like the IMF and World Bank suggest that at current growth trajectories, China will surpass US GDP in nominal terms in the coming decades.

Answer (b): While China's overall economy grew dramatically, the benefits were unevenly distributed for two key reasons. First, stark inequality developed between urban and rural populations. Economic reforms concentrated in Special Economic Zones and coastal cities like Shanghai and Shenzhen, which attracted foreign investment and industrial growth. Rural inland regions were largely left behind, with farmers receiving limited gains while urban workers in export industries prospered. Second, the dismantling of the old socialist welfare state — which had provided guaranteed employment, healthcare, and housing — left millions of workers without social security. As state-owned enterprises were privatised or restructured, millions of workers lost their guaranteed jobs, and only those with skills, capital, or connections to the new market economy could benefit.
questions.solution_hindi:
उत्तर (a): चीन की अर्थव्यवस्था के अमेरिका को पछाड़ने की संभावना के कई आधार हैं। 1978 में देंग शियाओपिंग के सुधारों के बाद से चीन ने लगातार उच्च आर्थिक विकास दर बनाए रखी है। चीन विश्व की सबसे बड़ी विनिर्माण अर्थव्यवस्था बन गया है और निर्यात आधारित विकास मॉडल अपनाया है। इसकी विशाल जनसंख्या सस्ती श्रम शक्ति और बढ़ता घरेलू बाजार प्रदान करती है।

उत्तर (b): चीन में सुधारों का लाभ सभी को नहीं मिला क्योंकि: प्रथम, तटीय शहरी क्षेत्रों और ग्रामीण अंतर्देशीय क्षेत्रों के बीच असमानता बढ़ी — शंघाई जैसे विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्रों में विदेशी निवेश केंद्रित हुआ जबकि ग्रामीण क्षेत्र पीछे रहे। द्वितीय, पुरानी समाजवादी कल्याण व्यवस्था — जो रोजगार, स्वास्थ्य सेवा और आवास की गारंटी देती थी — के समाप्त होने से लाखों मजदूरों ने सामाजिक सुरक्षा खो दी।

questions.text: "1960 के दशक को भारत में 'खतरनाक दशक' के रूप में चिह्नित किया गया है ।" इसके कोई दो कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: "The 1960s were labelled as the 'dangerous decade' in India." Explain any two reasons for this.

key_points: The 1962 India-China war revealed military and strategic vulnerabilities
Severe food shortages, drought, and economic difficulties threatened national stability
Regional and linguistic conflicts challenged national unity

questions.solution: The 1960s are described as the 'dangerous decade' in India due to several serious challenges that threatened the very stability of the young democracy. First, the India-China War of 1962 was a severe blow to India's national pride and strategic confidence. China's military invasion along the Himalayan border exposed India's military unpreparedness and diplomatic misjudgement. India suffered significant territorial losses and the war shattered the image of Sino-Indian brotherhood that Nehru had carefully cultivated. The defeat also destabilised Nehru's health and authority and raised serious doubts about India's security. Second, India faced acute food shortages and economic difficulties during this decade. Two consecutive droughts (1965 and 1966) combined with the disruption caused by two wars (with China in 1962 and Pakistan in 1965) created severe food scarcity. India was forced to depend on American food aid under the PL-480 programme, which compromised its sovereign foreign policy. These dual crises of security and economic survival gave the decade its 'dangerous' label.
questions.solution_hindi: 1960 के दशक को भारत में 'खतरनाक दशक' कहे जाने के दो प्रमुख कारण: प्रथम, 1962 का भारत-चीन युद्ध भारत की राष्ट्रीय प्रतिष्ठा के लिए गंभीर आघात था। हिमालयी सीमा पर चीन के सैन्य आक्रमण ने भारत की सैन्य तैयारी की कमजोरियों को उजागर किया। भारी क्षेत्रीय नुकसान हुआ और नेहरू की विदेश नीति पर गंभीर सवाल उठे। द्वितीय, लगातार दो सूखों (1965 और 1966) और दो युद्धों (चीन 1962 और पाकिस्तान 1965) के कारण भयंकर खाद्य संकट उत्पन्न हुआ। भारत को अमेरिकी खाद्य सहायता पर निर्भर होना पड़ा जिससे संप्रभु विदेश नीति प्रभावित हुई। इन दोनों संकटों ने इस दशक को 'खतरनाक' बना दिया।

questions.text: भारतीय संस्कृति पर वैश्वीकरण के प्रभाव का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe the impact of globalisation on the Indian culture.

key_points: Globalisation has led to cultural homogenisation — Western lifestyle, food habits, and fashion are displacing traditional Indian practices
It has created cultural hybridity where Indian and foreign elements blend
Indian culture has also spread globally through Yoga, Bollywood, cuisine, and IT professionals

questions.solution: Globalisation has had both positive and challenging impacts on Indian culture. On the challenging side, it has accelerated cultural homogenisation, where Western lifestyles, food habits such as fast food chains, English-medium education, and global fashion trends are increasingly replacing traditional Indian customs, languages, and dress. There is growing concern that traditional art forms, local crafts, and regional languages may lose their vitality under the pressure of globally dominant cultures. On the positive side, globalisation has created a vibrant cultural hybridity where Indian and global elements blend creatively — evident in fusion music, contemporary Indian cinema that incorporates global storytelling techniques, and modern art that draws on both traditions. Furthermore, Indian culture itself has gained global influence: Yoga has become a worldwide phenomenon, Bollywood films and Indian cuisine are popular across continents, and the Indian diaspora of IT professionals and academics has spread Indian intellectual and cultural heritage globally. Thus, globalisation is a double-edged process that simultaneously threatens cultural diversity and enables cultural exchange.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण का भारतीय संस्कृति पर सकारात्मक और नकारात्मक दोनों प्रकार का प्रभाव पड़ा है। नकारात्मक रूप से, इसने सांस्कृतिक एकरूपता को बढ़ावा दिया है जिसमें पाश्चात्य जीवनशैली, फास्ट फूड, अंग्रेजी शिक्षा और वैश्विक फैशन ट्रेंड पारंपरिक भारतीय रीति-रिवाजों, भाषाओं और वेशभूषा की जगह ले रहे हैं। परंतु सकारात्मक पक्ष यह है कि सांस्कृतिक संकरण भी हुआ है। भारतीय संस्कृति का भी वैश्विक प्रसार हुआ है — योग, बॉलीवुड, भारतीय व्यंजन और IT पेशेवरों के माध्यम से भारतीय संस्कृति विश्व भर में लोकप्रिय हो रही है। इस प्रकार वैश्वीकरण एक द्विधारी प्रक्रिया है।

questions.text:
(a) 1989 से भारत में गठबंधन राजनीति के एक लंबे दौर की शुरूआत के किन्हीं दो कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
अथवा
(b) भारतीय राजनीति में 'अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग' की भूमिका की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any two reasons for the beginning of a long phase of coalition politics in India since 1989.
OR
(b) Explain the role of 'Other Backward Classes' in the Indian politics.

key_points: (a) Fragmentation of the national political landscape with rise of regional parties
(a) Decline of the Congress as the dominant national party after its misuse of power
(b) The Mandal Commission report led to political mobilisation of OBC communities
(b) OBCs became a major vote bank and several regional parties emerged representing OBC interests

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Coalition politics in India since 1989 emerged due to two fundamental reasons. First, there was a significant fragmentation of the national political landscape caused by the rise of regional parties representing state-specific interests, caste groups, and linguistic communities. No single national party, not even the Congress, could win an outright majority in the Lok Sabha on its own. Regional parties such as the Telugu Desam Party, the AIADMK, the Samajwadi Party, and many others gained strength, making coalition-building necessary. Second, the Congress Party's prolonged dominance declined after the Emergency period due to its authoritarian excesses. Voters increasingly rejected single-party dominance and preferred multi-party competition. The rise of the BJP as an alternative national party further divided the national vote, ensuring that coalitions were required to form stable governments.

Answer (b): The Other Backward Classes (OBCs) have played a transformative role in Indian politics since the implementation of the Mandal Commission Report in 1990. The report's recommendation to reserve 27% of central government jobs for OBCs triggered enormous political mobilisation. Several regional parties — such as the Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, and Janata Dal — emerged as champions of OBC interests and built large electoral bases among these communities. OBCs, who constitute a substantial share of India's population, became a decisive vote bank. This shift democratised Indian politics by bringing previously marginalised communities into political power, producing OBC leaders as Chief Ministers and even Prime Ministers. The rising OBC assertion also led to intense caste-based competition among political parties vying for backward class support.

questions.text: भारत की परमाणु नीति की किन्हीं चार महत्वपूर्ण विशेषताओं को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any four important features of the Nuclear Policy of India.

key_points: No First Use policy — India will not use nuclear weapons first
Credible minimum deterrence — maintaining only enough nuclear weapons for deterrence
Non-use against non-nuclear states
Opposition to the discriminatory NPT and support for universal nuclear disarmament

questions.solution: India's nuclear policy has four important features. First, India follows a 'No First Use' (NFU) doctrine, which means it will not use nuclear weapons first in any conflict and will only retaliate with nuclear weapons if it is first attacked with nuclear weapons. This is a responsible restraint-based approach. Second, India maintains a policy of 'credible minimum deterrence,' meaning it possesses only the minimum number of nuclear weapons necessary to deter any adversary from launching a nuclear attack on India, rather than engaging in a nuclear arms race. Third, India commits to non-use of nuclear weapons against non-nuclear weapon states, which means it will not threaten or attack countries that do not possess nuclear weapons. Fourth, India has consistently opposed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as it is discriminatory — the NPT allows the five permanent members of the UN Security Council to retain nuclear weapons while prohibiting others. India calls for universal, non-discriminatory global nuclear disarmament.

(a) Explain any two commonalities and two differences between Bangladesh and Pakistan in their democratic experiences.
OR
(b) Explain any two issues of co-operation and two issues of confrontation between India and Bangladesh.

key_points: (a) Commonality 1: Both countries have experienced frequent military interventions and interruptions to civilian democratic rule
(a) Commonality 2: Both have faced difficulties in establishing stable democratic institutions due to weak political culture and social divisions
(a) Difference 1: Bangladesh has recently shown stronger democratic consolidation with relatively free elections compared to Pakistan
(a) Difference 2: Pakistan's military has a more institutionalised and dominant political role while Bangladesh's military returned to barracks after civilian pressure
(b) Cooperation: River water sharing (Ganga/Teesta), trade, and transit cooperation; collaboration on counter-terrorism
(b) Confrontation: Illegal immigration and border disputes; sharing of river waters (Teesta dispute); India's support for West Bengal parties viewed with suspicion

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Bangladesh and Pakistan share two important commonalities in their democratic experiences. First, both countries have suffered repeated military coups and prolonged periods of military rule that interrupted civilian democratic governance. Bangladesh experienced military rule under Ziaur Rahman and later H.M. Ershad, while Pakistan saw military dictators like Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf. Second, both nations have struggled to build robust democratic institutions, with weak rule of law, political instability, and a culture of confrontational politics hindering democratic consolidation. Two key differences are: first, Pakistan's military has become far more institutionalised as a political actor with an independent foreign policy agenda (especially regarding India and Afghanistan), whereas Bangladesh's military, though influential, has been more willing to return political power to civilians after crises. Second, Bangladesh has managed to alternate power more regularly between two major political parties — the Awami League and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party — through elections, while Pakistan has seen more fragmented democracy with the military consistently operating as a veto player behind the scenes.

Answer (b): India and Bangladesh cooperate on several important fronts. First, the two countries have made significant progress in trade relations, with India being one of Bangladesh's largest trading partners. Connectivity projects including rail and road links have been developed to improve regional integration and facilitate the movement of goods. Second, both countries cooperate on security issues, particularly in combating insurgencies in India's northeast; Bangladesh has taken significant steps to prevent its territory from being used by Indian insurgent groups. On the confrontation side, the issue of illegal immigration from Bangladesh into India — particularly into Assam and West Bengal — remains deeply contentious and has strained bilateral relations. Second, the sharing of river waters remains a persistent dispute: the Teesta River water-sharing agreement has been pending for years due to opposition from West Bengal's state government, causing frustration in Bangladesh.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): International organisations like the United Nations play an indispensable role in contemporary world politics. The United Nations, established in 1945, serves as the primary platform for maintaining international peace and security. Through its Security Council, it can authorise peacekeeping missions and sanctions against aggressors. The UN has deployed hundreds of peacekeeping operations in conflict zones across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, saving countless lives. Beyond security, the UN's specialised agencies — such as UNICEF, WHO, UNESCO, and the World Food Programme — address global challenges including poverty, disease, illiteracy, and hunger, making it a vital instrument of multilateral development cooperation. The UN also promotes and protects human rights through the Human Rights Council and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. As a forum for multilateral diplomacy, the UN's General Assembly provides every nation, regardless of size, an equal voice in global affairs. It helps negotiate international treaties on climate change, disarmament, and trade. In short, the UN prevents world conflicts from escalating and coordinates global responses to collective problems that no single nation can solve alone.

Answer (b): Four significant changes after the Cold War that have reshaped world politics: First, the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991 ended the bipolar world order. The Cold War competition between two superpowers gave way to a unipolar moment dominated by the United States. Second, the United States emerged as the world's sole superpower with unmatched military, economic, and cultural power, enabling it to pursue a strategy of hegemony and intervene in conflicts globally (Gulf War, Kosovo, Afghanistan, Iraq). Third, new regional powers began to emerge — China, India, the European Union, and Brazil — creating the conditions for a multipolar world that challenges US dominance and redistributes power across the globe. Fourth, non-state actors gained enormous influence in world politics. Terrorist organisations like Al-Qaeda demonstrated that non-state actors could challenge superpowers; international organisations like the WTO, IMF, and World Bank became key shapers of global economic governance, and multinational corporations gained power rivalling that of many governments.

अथवा
(b) जम्मू-कश्मीर से सम्बन्धित किन्हीं तीन समस्याओं की परख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) "Regional demands from different parts of India show that India has adopted a democratic approach to accommodate diversity." Justify the statement.
OR
(b) Examine any three problems related to the Jammu and Kashmir.

key_points: (a) India resolved linguistic demands through peaceful reorganisation of states on linguistic basis in 1956
(a) Tribal autonomy demands in Northeast India were addressed through creation of new states like Nagaland, Mizoram
(a) Demands for autonomy accommodated through federalism, special provisions like Article 371
(b) Pakistani-backed cross-border terrorism and militancy
(b) The issue of Kashmiri Pandits' exodus and their rehabilitation
(b) Political alienation and demands for greater autonomy or self-determination among sections of the population

questions.solution:
Answer (a): India's handling of regional demands demonstrates its fundamentally democratic approach to accommodating diversity rather than suppressing it by force. When linguistic communities demanded states reorganised along language lines, India established the States Reorganisation Commission in 1953 and enacted the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, creating linguistically defined states. This was a peaceful, democratic solution to a potentially explosive demand. When tribal communities in Nagaland, Mizoram, and Meghalaya demanded autonomy and recognition, India created new states for them rather than treating their aspirations as threats. The Mizo National Front, after years of armed struggle, reached a peace accord with the government in 1986, and Mizoram became a full state. Similarly, demands from Punjab for a Punjabi-speaking state were eventually met with the creation of Punjab and Haryana in 1966. Special provisions under Articles 371 and 370 (before abrogation) recognised the unique cultural and historical identity of specific regions. This pattern — dialogue, negotiation, constitutional accommodation — rather than military suppression, is what distinguishes India's democratic management of diversity.

Answer (b): Jammu and Kashmir faces three interconnected problems. First, Pakistani-sponsored cross-border terrorism and infiltration of militants have caused widespread violence, killed thousands of civilians, security personnel, and militants, and destabilised normal life in the Valley. The Line of Control remains a flashpoint, and Pakistan's support for armed groups continues to be a major security challenge. Second, the Valley has witnessed political alienation among sections of its population who feel their aspirations for greater autonomy, or in some cases self-determination, have not been adequately addressed. This alienation has been deepened by instances of human rights concerns and a feeling that democratic processes in the state have sometimes been manipulated. Third, the exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Valley in 1989-90 under threat from militants created a massive humanitarian crisis. Tens of thousands of Kashmiri Pandits fled their ancestral homeland and have been living as displaced persons, creating a serious issue of justice, rehabilitation, and communal reconciliation that remains unresolved.

उत्तर (b): जम्मू-कश्मीर की तीन प्रमुख समस्याएँ: प्रथम, पाकिस्तान-प्रायोजित सीमापार आतंकवाद और घुसपैठ जो व्यापक हिंसा का कारण बनी है। द्वितीय, कश्मीर घाटी में राजनीतिक अलगाव और स्वायत्तता की माँग — जनता के एक वर्ग को लगता है कि उनकी आकांक्षाओं को पर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं मिला। तृतीय, 1989-90 में कश्मीरी पंडितों का बड़े पैमाने पर पलायन एक गंभीर मानवीय संकट है जो पुनर्वास और सांप्रदायिक सुलह की दृष्टि से अभी भी अनसुलझा है।

अथवा
(b) 1949 में मणिपुर के भारत में विलय के लिए उत्तरदायी परिस्थितियों तथा संबंधित घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any three circumstances under which the State Reorganisation Commission was constituted.
OR
(b) Describe the circumstances and events that led to Manipur's accession to India in 1949.

key_points: (a) Strong agitations by linguistic communities for creation of states based on language
(a) Formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's death following a fast — this created pressure for a comprehensive reorganisation
(a) Fear that linguistic reorganisation would threaten national unity — yet failure to do so was also causing unrest
(b) Manipur's Maharaja signed the Instrument of Accession in 1949 under pressure
(b) Manipur had held elections in 1948 and formed a democratic government, but the central government pressed for merger
(b) The process of merger was controversial as it overrode the wishes of the elected legislature of Manipur

questions.solution:
Answer (a): The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was constituted in 1953 under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali due to three pressing circumstances. First, there were powerful agitations across the country by linguistic communities demanding that Indian states be reorganised along linguistic lines. The most intense agitation was in the Telugu-speaking regions of Madras State, where people demanded a separate Andhra Pradesh. The campaign was led by leaders including Potti Sriramulu, who undertook a fast unto death for this cause. Second, the death of Potti Sriramulu in December 1952 after a 56-day fast triggered widespread riots and political pressure that forced the government to create Andhra Pradesh in October 1953 as the first state formed on linguistic grounds. This partial solution made the demand for a comprehensive national reorganisation irresistible. Third, the Indian government itself recognised that the existing map of India — largely inherited from British administrative convenience — did not reflect the linguistic and cultural realities of the population. Unless a rational and systematic reorganisation was carried out, piecemeal demands would continue to destabilise the administration. The SRC was therefore tasked with recommending a comprehensive reorganisation of state boundaries.

Answer (b): Manipur's accession to India in 1949 was a complex process shaped by specific political circumstances. Manipur had been a princely state that acceded to India on 11 August 1947. However, it retained a degree of internal autonomy. In 1948, Manipur conducted elections to its legislative assembly — becoming one of the first places in independent India to hold democratic elections under a constitutional framework. A democratic government was formed and functioned for a period. The central government, however, was eager to fully integrate Manipur into the Indian Union. The Maharaja of Manipur, Bodhchandra Singh, was summoned to Shillong in September 1949 and presented with a Merger Agreement. Under considerable pressure from the Government of India, and reportedly without consulting his elected legislative assembly, the Maharaja signed the Merger Agreement on 21 September 1949. Manipur thereby became a Part C State of India. Many Manipuri people, including members of the elected assembly, felt that the merger bypassed democratic processes and overrode the wishes of the elected government. This sense of grievance contributed to long-standing feelings of alienation and later fuelled insurgent movements in the region demanding greater autonomy or independence.
questions.solution_hindi:
उत्तर (a): राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग (SRC) की स्थापना 1953 में जस्टिस फ़ज़ल अली की अध्यक्षता में तीन प्रमुख परिस्थितियों में हुई। प्रथम, भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों के पुनर्गठन की माँग को लेकर देशभर में शक्तिशाली आंदोलन चल रहे थे। सबसे तीव्र आंदोलन तेलुगुभाषी क्षेत्रों में था जो मद्रास राज्य से अलग आंध्र प्रदेश चाहते थे। द्वितीय, पोट्टि श्रीरामुलु की मृत्यु (दिसम्बर 1952) के बाद हुए दंगों ने सरकार को 1953 में आंध्र प्रदेश बनाने पर विवश किया जिससे व्यापक पुनर्गठन की माँग और प्रबल हो गई। तृतीय, सरकार स्वयं मानती थी कि ब्रिटिशकालीन प्रशासनिक सीमाएँ भाषाई-सांस्कृतिक वास्तविकताओं को नहीं दर्शाती थीं और खंडित माँगों से बेहतर एक व्यापक पुनर्गठन आवश्यक था।

उत्तर (b): मणिपुर का भारत में विलय जटिल परिस्थितियों में हुआ। मणिपुर ने 11 अगस्त 1947 को भारत में अधिमिलन किया था लेकिन आंतरिक स्वायत्तता बनाए रखी। 1948 में मणिपुर में चुनाव हुए और एक लोकतांत्रिक सरकार गठित हुई। इसके बावजूद केंद्र सरकार पूर्ण एकीकरण चाहती थी। सितम्बर 1949 में महाराजा बोधचंद्र सिंह को शिलांग बुलाया गया और विलय समझौते पर हस्ताक्षर के लिए दबाव डाला गया। 21 सितम्बर 1949 को निर्वाचित विधानसभा से परामर्श किए बिना विलय समझौते पर हस्ताक्षर हुए। इस प्रक्रिया ने मणिपुरी जनता में अलगाव की भावना को जन्म दिया जो बाद में विद्रोही आंदोलनों का आधार बनी।
